tests.title: A workspace's repository name is derived and collision-free
given: a set of workspaces with slugs that differ only in case, in hyphens and in length
tests.when: the repository name is computed for each, twice
then: each workspace yields the same name on both computations
no two workspaces yield the same name
the name is valid for the store's naming rules
tests.pseudocode: in the repository naming test file: assert name(ws) == name(ws); assert len({name(w) for w in workspaces}) == len(workspaces)

tests.title: Creating a workspace creates its repository
given: a store with no repositories
tests.when: a workspace is created
then: the store holds a repository under the workspace's derived name once the create route has answered
a second workspace adds a second repository and leaves the first alone
tests.pseudocode: in the repository store integration test file: post(workspace); assert store.exists(name(ws))

tests.title: Refs and objects survive a restart of the service
given: a workspace whose repository holds two branches and a tag
tests.when: every component but the store is restarted and the repository is read again
then: every ref is present at the same commit
the objects are readable
no re-copy from the remote happened
tests.pseudocode: in the repository store integration test file: before = refs(ws); restart_service(); assert refs(ws) == before and remote.fetch_count == 1

tests.title: Two writes to one workspace's repository are serialised
given: a workspace and two operations that write its repository and record their start and end instants
tests.when: both are started concurrently on the same workspace, and then one on each of two workspaces
then: on one workspace the intervals do not overlap
a writer that may not wait answers 409 workspace_busy
writes to different workspaces may overlap
tests.pseudocode: in the repository store integration test file: run concurrently and assert not overlapping(a, b) for one workspace

tests.title: A copy brings every branch and tag at the right commit
given: a remote with three branches, two tags and a non-default HEAD
tests.when: a workspace is created for it and the copy completes
then: all three branches and both tags exist in the workspace's repository
each is at the same commit as on the remote
HEAD points where the remote's HEAD points
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file: assert refs(ws) == refs(remote) and head(ws) == head(remote)

tests.title: A private remote is copied with the stored credential, which never leaks
given: a private remote that requires a token, and a workspace created with that token as git_pat
tests.when: the copy runs
then: the copy succeeds and the workspace reaches ready
the remote saw the token
the token appears in no response body and no log record
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file: assert status(ws) == 'ready' and remote.sawToken == tok and tok not in logs.text

tests.title: A public remote needs no credential and a private one without a credential fails
given: a public remote and a private remote
workspaces created for each with no credential
tests.when: each copy runs
then: the public one reaches ready and the remote saw no credential
the private one ends at failed with clone_error set
neither leaves the workspace unreadable
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file, table over (remoteVisibility, expectedStatus)

tests.title: Credentials the remote refuses stop the create before anything is written
given: a remote that refuses a particular token
tests.when: a workspace is created with that token
then: the create answers 400
no workspace row, no secret and no repository exists afterwards
the message does not contain the token
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file: r = post(workspace, badTok); assert r.status == 400 and not exists(ws) and not store.exists(name(ws)) and badTok not in r.text

tests.title: A copy that fails after creation leaves a readable failed workspace
given: a remote that accepts the credential check and then fails the transfer, one that disappears, and one that refuses after creation
tests.when: a workspace is created for each and each copy runs
then: each workspace ends at failed with clone_error naming the failure
each workspace is still readable and can be archived
no clone_error contains a credential
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file, table over the three failure modes asserting status, clone_error and that read and archive still work

tests.title: A copy larger than one unit of work continues and completes
given: a remote whose transfer cannot finish within one unit of platform work
tests.when: a workspace is created for it and the copy runs to completion
then: the workspace reaches ready
every branch of the remote is present
the copy was resumed at least once rather than restarted from the beginning
tests.pseudocode: in the copy-in integration test file: create(bigRemote); assert eventually(status == 'ready') and refs(ws) == refs(remote) and resumeCount >= 1

tests.title: The status sequence and head_sha follow the copy
given: a workspace being created for a reachable remote and one for an unreachable remote
tests.when: the workspace is polled throughout the copy
then: the observed statuses are a prefix of pending, cloning, ready for the first and of pending, cloning, failed for the second
head_sha is null before ready and a 40-character hex string after
no status outside the four appears
tests.pseudocode: in the clone status integration test file: seq = poll_until_terminal(); assert is_prefix(seq, ['pending','cloning','ready'])

tests.title: A workspace does not stay in cloning for ever
given: a copy that hangs without failing, and a controllable clock
tests.when: the clock is advanced past 30 minutes with the workspace still in cloning
then: the workspace moves to failed with clone_error set
the clone_error says the copy timed out
the workspace can then be recloned or archived
tests.pseudocode: in the clone status integration test file: start_hanging_copy(); clock.advance(31*60); assert status(ws) == 'failed' and clone_error is not None

tests.title: Reactivating a workspace whose repository was kept reuses it
given: an archived workspace whose archive push failed, so its repository was kept, holding a branch that exists on no remote
tests.when: the workspace is reactivated and reaches ready
then: the branch that exists on no remote is still present
no transfer from the remote happened
the workspace reaches ready
tests.pseudocode: in the clone status integration test file: post(reactivate); assert eventually(status == 'ready') and localOnlyBranch in refs(ws) and remote.fetch_count == before

tests.title: The store's three undocumented capabilities are established by exercising them
given: a real store and a scratch repository
tests.when: a ref outside refs/heads/ and refs/tags/ is pushed, a non-fast-forward update is pushed, and a ref deletion is pushed
then: each attempt yields a definite supported or unsupported result
the capability report matches what each attempt did
the report is derived from the attempts and not from a hard-coded table
tests.pseudocode: in the store capability integration test file: for cap in CAPS: observed = attempt(cap); assert store.capabilities()[cap] == observed

tests.title: An operation needing a missing capability fails and names it
given: a store implementation reporting each capability as unsupported in turn
tests.when: an operation requiring that capability is attempted
then: the operation fails
the error names the missing capability
the repository is unchanged, and no different effect was applied in its place
tests.pseudocode: in the store capability test file, table over the three capabilities asserting the failure, the message and an unchanged ref list

tests.title: A repository at the stated size limits is copied, read and written
given: a remote with 500 MB of packed objects and one with 10000 refs
tests.when: each is copied in, read back and written to
then: each reaches status ready
every ref is readable afterwards
a subsequent write succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the repository size integration test file, skipping with a named reason when the fixture cannot be built: assert status == 'ready' and len(refs(ws)) == 10000

tests.title: An operation past the store's limit fails cleanly and leaves the workspace usable
given: a workspace near the store's storage limit
tests.when: a write that would exceed the limit is attempted
then: the operation fails with the documented storage-failure answer
the message names the limit exceeded
the workspace is still readable and its earlier refs are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the repository size integration test file: r = write_over_limit(); assert r.failed and 'limit' in r.message and refs(ws) == before

tests.title: The origin credential follows the documented order
given: workspaces holding every combination of GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME and GIT_PASSWORD
tests.when: the origin credential is resolved for each
then: GIT_PAT wins when present, even alongside a complete basic pair
a complete basic pair is used when there is no GIT_PAT
no credential is produced when neither is present
tests.pseudocode: in the credential resolution test file, table over the eight combinations asserting the resolved credential

tests.title: The upstream credential falls back to the origin credential
given: workspaces holding every combination of the upstream names and the origin names
tests.when: the upstream credential is resolved for each
then: UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT wins when present
the upstream basic pair is used when there is no upstream token
with no upstream secret at all the origin credential is used
with neither upstream nor origin credential none is produced
tests.pseudocode: in the credential resolution test file, table over the combinations asserting the resolved upstream credential

tests.title: A half basic pair is ignored and the fact is recorded
given: a workspace holding GIT_USERNAME without GIT_PASSWORD, and one holding GIT_PASSWORD without GIT_USERNAME
a recording log sink
tests.when: the origin credential is resolved for each
then: the resolution falls through as though neither half existed
a log record says the half pair was ignored
no log record contains the value of the half that was present
tests.pseudocode: in the credential resolution test file: assert resolve(ws) is None and 'ignored' in sink.text and value not in sink.text

tests.title: Only the workspace's own scope is read for the reserved names
given: a workspace with no GIT_PAT, whose owner has GIT_PAT at user scope and whose organization has GIT_PAT at organization scope
tests.when: the origin credential is resolved
then: no credential is produced
neither the user's nor the organization's value is used
adding GIT_PAT at the workspace scope then produces it
tests.pseudocode: in the credential resolution integration test file: assert resolve(ws) is None; set_workspace_secret('GIT_PAT', v); assert resolve(ws) == v

tests.title: Archiving pushes every branch to origin and then releases the repository
given: a ready workspace with a usable origin credential and a branch that exists only in its repository
tests.when: the workspace is archived
then: the branch exists on origin afterwards
the repository is released from the store
the workspace's status is archived
tests.pseudocode: in the repository retirement integration test file: post(archive); assert localOnlyBranch in refs(remote) and not store.exists(name(ws))

tests.title: A failed archive push keeps the repository rather than losing commits
given: a ready workspace with a branch that exists only in its repository, and a remote that refuses the push
a second workspace with no usable credential
tests.when: each is archived
then: both reach status archived
both repositories are still in the store with the local-only branch present
reactivating either reuses the kept repository
tests.pseudocode: in the repository retirement integration test file, table over the two cases asserting status, store.exists and the branch's presence

tests.title: Deleting a workspace removes its repository
given: an archived workspace whose repository was kept
tests.when: the workspace is deleted
then: the store holds no repository under that workspace's derived name
the delete answers 204
tests.pseudocode: in the repository retirement integration test file: delete(ws); assert not store.exists(name(ws))

tests.title: The repository store contract suite passes against both implementations
given: the repository store contract suite, the Cloudflare implementation over Artifacts and the non-Cloudflare implementation
tests.when: the suite is run against each
then: every case passes against both
the suite is one definition run twice, parameterised only by the implementation
a case that passes against one and fails against the other is reported as a failure
tests.pseudocode: in the repository store contract test file: for impl in [artifactsImpl(), localImpl()]: runContractSuite(impl)

tests.title: No store token reaches a response or a log
given: a store implementation that mints a distinctive repo-scoped token
a recording log sink
tests.when: a copy, a read, a failed write and a request that raises an unhandled failure are each performed
then: no response body contains the token
no log record contains it
the operations themselves still succeed, so the token was used and not merely withheld
tests.pseudocode: in the repository store test file: for scenario in SCENARIOS: run(scenario); assert TOKEN not in body and TOKEN not in sink.text

tests.title: A private repository is registered and reaches ready against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a real store, and a private remote with a working token
tests.when: a workspace is created with that token and polled until its status is terminal
then: the create answers 201 with status pending
the workspace reaches ready with head_sha set
every branch of the remote is present in the workspace's repository
the token appears in no response
tests.pseudocode: in the repository smoke test file: post(workspace, git_pat=tok); assert poll_until_terminal() == 'ready' and head_sha is not None

tests.title: A failed copy leaves a readable workspace that says why
given: a running deployment and a remote that becomes unreachable after the credential check
tests.when: a workspace is created for it and polled until its status is terminal
then: the create answers 201
the workspace reaches failed with clone_error naming the failure
the workspace is still readable and can be archived
clone_error contains no credential
tests.pseudocode: in the repository smoke test file: post(workspace); assert poll_until_terminal() == 'failed' and read().json.clone_error

tests.title: Archiving pushes branches out and deleting removes the repository
given: a running deployment, a ready workspace with a branch that exists only in its repository, and a writable remote
tests.when: the workspace is archived and then deleted
then: the branch exists on the remote after the archive
the workspace's status is archived
after the delete the store holds no repository for it
tests.pseudocode: in the repository smoke test file: post(archive); assert branch in remote_refs(); delete(ws); assert not store_has(ws)
